properties.label: Kairouan Plain · Chebika
properties.description: A window on the semi-arid Kairouan plain near the Chebika research area, where remote sensing has been studied for irrigation mapping.

evidence.title: Soil Moisture and Irrigation Mapping in a Semi-Arid Region
evidence.limitation: The paper studies satellite irrigation mapping. The app's independent WorldCover layer maps land-cover classes and does not identify recent irrigation.

source.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90
source.attribution: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-90 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved
source.coverage: 33 × 33 samples over ~10 km per axis; sampled surface heights in metres, ~90 m native DEM, 2021 release.

source.name: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200
source.attribution: © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by ESA WorldCover consortium
source.coverage: Categorical 10 m land cover in the profile window. The 3D texture shows the dominant class in each coarser cell. Class shares use the original valid pixels, including water.

source.name: NASA POWER daily
source.coverage: MERRA-2 and SYN1DEG gridded data for the requested point. UTC complete-day means for temperature and irradiance, precipitation summed over the same days.

location_source.name: Study-window reference point
location_source.coverage: Reference point for an approximately 10 × 10 km evidence window. The window is not a cadastral or study-area boundary.

water_question: Which field observations would let us tell recent irrigation from rainfall or land-cover differences?
missing_inputs: Parcel boundaries and current crop calendars
